passage: Consumers often assume that adding more options to a menu or product line invariably increases satisfaction and sales. Yet behavioral economists have repeatedly demonstrated the paradox of choice, in which an abundance of alternatives overwhelms cognitive capacity and triggers decision paralysis. When faced with dozens of nearly identical varieties, shoppers expend significant mental energy comparing minor attributes and worry intensely about making a suboptimal selection. Consequently, many walk away without purchasing anything at all, or experience lingering regret after choosing because they imagine the unchosen alternatives might have been superior. By curating a smaller, well-structured set of distinct options, businesses reduce mental friction, build buyer confidence, and frequently achieve higher conversion rates and greater customer loyalty.
